claim: Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes to Dol-de-Bretagne is approximately 16 km by road, around 20 minutes by car.
quote: The distance between Dol-de-Bretagne and Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes is approximately 16 kilometers by road. It generally takes approximately 20 minutes to cover this distance by car.

claim: The Menhir du Champ-Dolent stands 9.3–9.5 m above ground, is the second largest standing stone in Brittany, weighs about 100 tonnes, and sits 2 km south of Dol on the D795.
quote: height above ground is between 9.3 and 9.5 metres ... second largest standing stone in Brittany, made of pinkish granite ... estimated weight of around 100 tonnes ... 2 kilometres south of Dol-de-Bretagne ... near the D795 road.

claim: Legend says the Champ-Dolent menhir sprang from the earth to separate two warring brothers, hence 'Field of Sorrow'.
quote: According to legend, the menhir rose from the ground to separate two feuding brothers who were on the point of killing each other ... 'Champ Dolent' which means 'Field of Sorrow'.

claim: Cathédrale Saint-Samson was founded in the 6th century, rebuilt after a 1203 fire, and its choir window of 1280–1290 is the oldest monumental stained glass in Brittany still in situ.
quote: founded in the sixth century by Saint Samson, a Welsh monk ... rebuilt after the fire of 1203 ... The main window of the choir, dating from the years 1280-1290, is the oldest monumental stained glass window in Brittany still preserved in situ.

claim: The Cathédraloscope at 4 place de la cathédrale, Dol-de-Bretagne charges €8.50 adult (audio guide included), €6.50 for 6–18, free under 6, and €26 for a 2-adult+2-child family pass.
quote: Adults: €8.50 (includes €2.00 audio guide); Children (6-18 years): €6.50; Children under 6: Free; Family package (2 adults + 2 children): €26.00

claim: Cathédraloscope opens daily 10:00–13:00 / 14:00–18:00 from 1 April; July–August daily 10:00–18:30; stone-carving workshops Tue/Wed/Thu from 9 July.
quote: From April 1st: Daily 10am-1pm / 2pm-6pm. July/August: Daily 10am-6:30pm ... Stone carving workshops are open from July 9th, on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays at 2pm, 3:30pm and 5pm.

claim: Château de Combourg reopens 1 April 2026; tickets €13.70 adult, €10.70 reduced, €5.70 ages 5–12 (château + park); park-only €4.70; 45-minute guided interior tour.
quote: Réouverture du château le 1er avril 2026! ... Adults: €13.70 ... Children (5-12 years): €5.70 ... Reduced rate: €10.70 ... Park Access Only: Adults: €4.70 ... Guided Tour Duration: 45 minutes

claim: Combourg is closed Saturdays all day and Sunday mornings outside school holidays; François-René de Chateaubriand spent his childhood here and immortalised it in 'Mémoires d'Outre-Tombe'.
quote: closed on Saturday all day and Sunday morning except during school holidays and bridge weekends ... François-René de Chateaubriand spent his childhood here and immortalized it in his 'Mémoires d'Outre-Tombe'.

claim: Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes to Combourg is roughly 33.8 km / 37 minutes via D73 and D76 (other sources give ~28 km).
quote: The drive from Combourg to Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes takes 37 minutes for a distance of 33.8 kilometers. The route is mainly via D 73 and D 76.

claim: Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes to Dinan is about 30.8 km, 29 minutes by car via N176 and D76.
quote: Distance: The distance to travel is calculated at 30.8 kilometres. Driving Time: ... 29 minutes. Route: ... mainly via N 176 and D 76.

claim: Dinan is encircled by nearly 3 km of ramparts, has a 14th-century château over the Rance, and harbours more than 130 half-timbered houses.
quote: Dinan is enclosed by nearly three kilometres of ramparts, and its 14th-century castle proudly overlooks the Rance river ... home to over 130 half-timbered houses.

claim: Place des Merciers is the heart of Dinan's historic centre, lined with half-timbered houses with ground-floor wooden porches, and a walk beyond the walls leads down to the old port on the Rance.
quote: The heart of Dinan's historic center is Place des Merciers, still lined with picturesque half-timbered buildings, many sporting ground-floor wooden porches ... A short walk beyond the walls leads down to the river and the city's once-thriving old port.

claim: Mont-Dol summit (65 m) offers a panorama over the Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel and the Dol marshes; the Tour Notre-Dame (blessed 1857) can be climbed and a Chapelle de l'Espérance sits at its base.
quote: Mont-Dol offers one of the most beautiful panoramas ... at an altitude of 65 metres ... The Tour Notre-Dame was blessed in 1857, and you can climb to the top of this tower ... Chapelle de l'Espérance with its small stone campanile
